TENDRA-H1 · Parametric robotic hand

Engineered to Move Like You

A 25-joint, tendon-driven hand generated by one Python script in Blender. Explode it, pose it and inspect every part, live in your browser.

Built around the human hand

Real Anatomy.
Real Engineering.

Link lengths come from adult hand anthropometry. Joint limits follow human range of motion, with hyperextension capped at 5–15°. The thumb sits on its own CMC ball joint, so it truly opposes instead of acting as a fifth finger.

Exploded by design

Every Part,
Pulled Apart

The exploded view isn't a random scatter. Each part travels by its depth in the kinematic chain, so fingertips fly furthest and the palm barely moves. Pins, bearings and screws slide out along their own hinge axes, the way a service manual shows an assembly.

Grasp taxonomy

Six Grasps.
Zero Collisions.

Open, Fist, Pinch, Point, Power Grip and OK Sign come from robotic grasp research. The thumb's opposition angles were found by a forward-kinematics search, and every preset passes an automated BVH interference check against the real part geometry.

hand_generator.py

TENDRA-H1
“Parametric Generator”

Nothing was modelled by hand. Change the scale, finger length, palm width or finger count and the script rebuilds every link, joint, tendon, label and driver, then re-verifies it. The three-finger gripper on the left came out of the same file.

Datasheet

What It Would
Take to Build

Datasheet (PDF)

Mass is each mesh's measured volume × its material density; motors use catalogue mass. Cost uses prototype quantities: MJF-printed PA12-CF links, machined titanium and aluminium, and off-the-shelf bearings and gearmotors.
